identity.title: Reducing Belief Deviation in Reinforcement Learning for Active Reasoning of LLM Agents

problem.claim: LLM agents performing multi-turn active reasoning can drift from the true problem state, causing uninformative or repetitive actions and compounding RL trajectory errors.

contributions.claim: Introduces T^3, which tracks belief deviation, detects excessive deviation, and truncates training trajectories to reduce uninformative tail effects.
Reports improved training stability, performance gains of up to 30 points, and token-cost reductions of up to 34% across five challenging tasks.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors characterize T^3 as a simple yet principled approach to controlling belief deviation during RL training.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that T^3 consistently enhances training stability across five challenging tasks.
The authors report performance improvements of up to 30 points and token-cost reductions of up to 34%.

narrative_sequence.summary: Active reasoning requires multi-turn interaction with external sources and strategic information gathering.
Accurate belief tracking is central, but limited reasoning can cause belief deviation and state-awareness loss.
Deviation can produce repetitive actions and corrupt RL credit assignment and exploration through compounding trajectory errors.
T^3 tracks deviation and truncates trajectories after excessive deviation, aiming to preserve informative prefixes.
The authors report stability, performance, and token-cost gains across five tasks.

source_observation.claim: The abstract links a recognizable trajectory failure mode—belief deviation—to a targeted intervention that truncates only excessively deviated tails while preserving informative prefixes.

lessons.interpretation: A strong abstract can align the intervention’s scope with the diagnosed failure mechanism and explain the intended credit-assignment effect.
lessons.application: When a sequential learning process becomes corrupted after a detectable state signal, define that signal and describe a localized intervention that preserves earlier informative computation.
lessons.exception: This framing is unsuitable when degradation cannot be localized, detected reliably, or separated from genuinely informative late-stage behavior.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify baselines, task identities, metric definitions, statistical variation, or whether the reported gains are relative to particular methods.
The detection criterion and trajectory-truncation procedure are not described in enough detail to assess implementation or reproducibility.
